notes:
Enterprise account. Very security-sensitive; procurement will not proceed without clear change control story.

Primary thread: change controls around route-level configuration updates (esp. Quantization Profile Library toggles) + audit logging completeness.

Key stakeholders (FalconBank):
- InfoSec reviewer: asked repeatedly for "who changed what, when, and what the previous value was" for route config.
- Risk/Compliance: wants audit log export to Splunk + retention policy documented.
- Platform Eng: wants deterministic behavior + explicit rollback path.

Requirements / asks (captured in 2025-03-12 security review):
- Audit logging: 
  - Must emit events for enable/disable quantization per route AND profile reference changes.
  - Event must include actor identity, auth method, request id, route id/name, model id/variant, previous vs new setting, and resolution outcome (applied vs fallback vs disabled).
  - Wants ability to export audit logs (API or batch export) to SIEM (Splunk). Asked if we can include quant_profile_id in exporter fields.
- RBAC and approval workflow:
  - They want a 4-eyes (maker/checker) style approval for any production route config change.
  - Redwood Console supports RBAC + audit trail, but no native multi-approver workflow today. Proposed compensating control: restrict permissions to a small admin group + enforce approvals via FalconBank change management (ServiceNow) and execute changes via Terraform/API with recorded ticket id in change description.
  - They asked whether the Console can require an "approval reason" field; we said we can log change reason in audit event (if provided) and recommend their internal process.
- Quantization Profile Library specifics:
  - They like that it is opt-in and route-level (not a hidden global default).
  - Asked about preventing silent changes when "recommended" aliases move; they want pinned versions only (explicit profile_id/version). Not comfortable with "latest" or auto-updating profiles.
  - Wants a tenant-level global disable as a safety net (in addition to route toggles) + emergency kill switch behavior documented.
  - Asked about deterministic selection across regions and dedicated pools; needs assurance that resolved profile ref is stable for a given route config + deployment tier.
- Data handling:
  - EU data residency required for inference traffic and logs.
  - Retention controls required (audit logs 1 year; request logs subject to stricter retention).
  - Key management: preference for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration) for Private deployment.

Technical notes / open items:
- Provide sample audit event schema and confirm fields available for export (including quant_profile_id, route identifiers, actor, diff).
- Confirm whether change history UI can be exported or accessed via API for compliance reporting.
- Validate that policy fallback behavior is always baseline precision when profile incompatible and that fallback emits a metric/event (they want alerting on fallback_rate).

Buying process:
- They are in procurement but waiting on security sign-off. Procurement team asked for SOC 2 report + ISO statement, plus a short "change control" memo for production operations.

Internal Redwood notes:
- This account is a good fit for Private (VPC) + Dedicated fallback. Quantization Profile Library is a key cost lever they want, but only if governance story is strong.
- Action: loop in Naomi Feldman (RBAC/audit requirements) + Kevin Osei (audit log export/SIEM) for the next security follow-up; Markus to run an implementation workshop with their platform team.

Last call quote (paraphrased): "We can accept opt-in optimization features, but we can’t accept an optimization knob that changes behavior without a clear approval trail and an immediate kill switch."
